articles.title: Understanding Computing Instructors' Perceptions of Student Sense of Belonging
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.13237v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Students' sense of belonging has been described as a feeling of community acceptance, respect, inclusion, and membership. In computing, student belonging is shaped by psychological, social, academic, and environmental factors, including their relationships with instructors. However, despite prior work emphasizing instructors' influence on student belonging, limited research has examined how computing instructors perceive, understand, and attempt to support belonging. articles.title: Developing an Operational Model for an Internet of Data Based Trusted Data Space for Vocational Education
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.13520v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Data circulation in vocational education has long been constrained by unclear ownership, a lack of trust, and insufficient incentives. The Internet of Data provides a new underlying technology for enabling trusted cross-domain data circulation. Building on an Internet of Data based trusted data space for vocational education, this paper develops a multi-stakeholder operational model encompassing a value network, a product portfolio, revenue allocation, and governance rules. articles.title: Repertoires of Contention: Building computational tools and infrastructures for community resistance to bitcoin mining
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.13527v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent work in human-computer interaction and allied fields has sought to engage community members as co-designers, facilitators, and decision makers to challenge structural power barriers and knowledge gaps. In this paper, we apply a diverse set of computational techniques to engage and address community concerns surrounding the socio-environmental impacts of the Greenidge Bitcoin mining power plant facility in upstate New York. articles.title: Perspicacious: An Educational Intelligence Platform for Instructional Designers
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.13549v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Designing effective instruction requires instructional designers to create assessment questions aligned with clearly defined knowledge components (KCs). These KCs represent specific knowledge or skills that students must acquire. This process is often time-consuming and relies heavily on expert labor. articles.title: Transparency Disclosures for Chain-of-Thought Monitorability
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.13873v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Chain-of-thought (CoT) monitoring is one of the most valuable tools for monitoring advanced AI systems, but it is under threat. We argue that frontier AI developers should report specific indicators to make these threats trackable and to better facilitate coordination to preserve CoT monitorability. We identify five indicators that are both highly relevant and reasonably feasible to disclose, one for each link in a five-step chain on which CoT monitoring depends. articles.title: Advancing a Global Framework for AI Safety and Governance for the Well-being of Humanity
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.13968v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Report "Advancing a Global Framework for AI Safety and Governance for the Well-being of Humanity" is an important outcome of the AI Safety and Governance Program of World Internet Conference Specialized Committee on Artificial Intelligence in 2025. articles.summary: arXiv:2611.14288v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Although large language models have demonstrated strong performance on algorithmic and mathematical tasks, their suitability as social science research assistants remains unclear, particularly because many social science questions lack agreed-upon, quantifiable benchmark answers. Evaluating this suitability is important since researchers and students increasingly rely on AI to generate research ideas. articles.title: Trust, but verify, audit and attribute: a human-in-the-loop framework for checking AI-produced research results
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.13042v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) systems now produce research results in bulk: in October 2026 a single laboratory released more than 700 AI-generated mathematics manuscripts, only part of them with machine-checked proofs. articles.title: Reliability of Claude Code as an Agentic AI Grading System for Handwritten University Exams
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.13217v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This study examines the reliability of Claude Code, an agentic deployment of the Claude Opus 4.6 large language model, as a grading system for handwritten university exams. Four research questions addressed agreement with expert human grading on total scores (RQ1), agreement across five question types from multiple choice to evaluative judgement (RQ2), consistency across two independent grading sessions one week apart (RQ3), and the accuracy of AI-generated feedback (RQ4). articles.title: Measuring Definition Sensitivity in LLM Annotation of Social Science Concepts
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.13339v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In social science research, text annotation is a fundamental task that is traditionally a costly, hard-to-scale manual process. Researchers have used large language models (LLMs) to perform annotation by writing a definition of a concept into a prompt - a rule that determines whether a label should be attributed to a text depending on its content.
